newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA TO LIFT IMPORT RESTRICTIONS ON NEW TYRES.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA TO LIFT IMPORT RESTRICTIONS ON NEW TYRES.

text.p: Quantitative restrictions on the import of new pneumatic tyres and inner tubes into South Africa would be lifted in January 1997, the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said on Thursday.
Restrictions on used tyres would, however, remain, the DTI said in a statement.

It said new imported tyres would have to comply with the minimum standards for passenger vehicles set by the South African Bureau of Standards in 1996 and those to be imposed on commercial vehicles in 1997.
Import permits would continue to be issued -- mainly for the purpose of monitoring the process, the DTI said.
The DTI said now that import restrictions had been lifted, the restructuring of import tariffs on tyres and tubes could take place.

It said the South African Tyre Manufacturers Conference earlier this month submitted a proposal urging an increase in 1997 in the ad valorem duty from 25 percent to 43 percent. The conference suggested this be followed by a phase-down to 30 percent by 2002.
